# Motion Graphics — HyperFrames

💳 Curated by Skill Harbor — a dispatch entry for short, design-led motion graphics where motion is the message: kinetic typography, stat count-ups, chart/data-viz hits, logo stings and brand lockups, lower thirds and callouts, animated maps, animated tweets/news cards, webpage/UI animation, or fusing a real image's geometry into a chart — usually under 10 seconds, no narration, rendered to MP4 or transparent overlay. Runs an autonomous pipeline (init, plan, source, design, build, verify, approve, render) around real assets, reusing HyperFrames catalog blocks and the shared motion vocabulary, with lint/check gates and proof snapshots before the render. Depends on the HyperFrames domain skills (kept fresh via `npx hyperframes skills update`); a Google API key (GEMINI_API_KEY / GOOGLE_API_KEY) is mentioned for image generation in asset-sourcing categories — without it those categories degrade to search-only. Distinct from the published HeyGen fiches in the catalog (music-to-video, talking-head-recut, figma, registry, studio): this one is a motion-design skill, not a talking-head/avatar workflow. Requires macOS Apple Silicon or Linux x64 with Node and ffmpeg. By @heygen-com, listed here with credit to its creator. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use.
